# x402 Mesh Inference

> A decentralized pay-per-prompt AI compute marketplace. It exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat
> completions endpoint that charges $0.0020 USDC per request over the x402 protocol on
> Algorand, then routes the prompt to a community GPU node and pays that node's operator
> $0.0017 USDC. No account, no API key, no subscription — an autonomous agent with a funded
> Algorand wallet can call it on its own.

You are probably reading this because you are an agent that needs LLM inference and can pay for
it. Everything you need is below.

## The one endpoint you care about

    POST https://mesh.example.com/v1/chat/completions

Request and response bodies are OpenAI-compatible: `{ "model", "messages", "max_tokens",
"temperature", "top_p", "stop", "stream" }` in, a `chat.completion` object out. Fields this
gateway does not implement are ignored rather than rejected, so an unmodified OpenAI SDK works
if you can attach the payment header.

Set `"stream": true` to get `text/event-stream` back: newline-delimited `data:` frames, each a
JSON `chat.completion.chunk`, terminated by the literal frame `data: [DONE]`.

## Price

$0.0020 USDC per request, flat, regardless of token count.

On the wire that is the string `"2000"` — x402 amounts are **integer atomic units**, and USDC
has 6 decimals on Algorand. Of every request: `2000` atomic units in, `1700` paid out to the
node operator that served you, `300` retained by the gateway. The invariant
`inbound - payout = margin` is enforced in code and published per request at
`GET /v1/settlements`.

## How to pay (x402, `exact` scheme, Algorand)

1. `POST /v1/chat/completions` with your normal body and **no** payment header.
   You get `402 Payment Required` and a JSON body:

   ```json
   {
     "x402Version": 2,
     "error": "X-PAYMENT header is required",
     "resource": { "url": "https://mesh.example.com/v1/chat/completions" },
     "accepts": [
       {
         "scheme": "exact",
         "network": "algorand:wGHE2Pwdvd7S12BL5FaOP20EGYesN73k",
         "asset": "31566704",
         "amount": "2000",
         "payTo": "<the gateway's Algorand address>",
         "maxTimeoutSeconds": 120,
         "extra": {
           "name": "USDC",
           "decimals": 6,
           "feePayer": "ZMFK2OI7ZBD2U27ISERZC4S6LKM6WMFJPZQ4MYNJDZ2VNBNMBA67RA22AA"
         }
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

2. Build the payment for the `accepts[0]` entry you selected. On Algorand the `exact` scheme
   uses an **atomic transaction group**: the facilitator's fee-payer transaction plus your USDC
   asset transfer. Both commit or neither does. Because `extra.feePayer` sponsors the ALGO
   network fee, the payment is **gasless for you** — you sign only the USDC transfer leg.

3. Re-send the identical request with the header:

       X-PAYMENT: base64(JSON PaymentPayload)

   where `PaymentPayload` is `{ "x402Version": 2, "accepted": <the accepts[] entry you chose>,
   "payload": { "paymentGroup": ["<base64 msgpack txn>", ...], "paymentIndex": 0 } }`.

4. You get `200` with the completion, plus a `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` response header containing
   base64 JSON with the confirmed Algorand transaction id.

The easiest way to do all of this is the reference client:

    npm install @x402/core @x402/avm
    import { x402Client } from "@x402/core/client";
    import { ExactAvmScheme } from "@x402/avm/exact/client";

## Prerequisites you will hit if you skip them

Algorand is opt-in. **Your wallet must opt in to the USDC ASA before you can hold or send it**
(asset id `31566704` on MainNet, `10458941` on TestNet). An opt-in is a zero-amount asset
transfer to yourself. You also need a minimum balance in ALGO: 0.1 ALGO for the account plus
0.1 ALGO per opted-in asset. Without the opt-in your payment will fail, not silently succeed.

## Models

Whatever the currently registered nodes advertise. Query it, do not guess:

    GET /v1/nodes?healthy=true

Each node lists `capabilities[]` with `model`, `contextWindow`, an optional `quantization`, and
the operator's quoted `pricePer1kTokensUsdc`. Typical entries are open-weight chat models served
by Ollama or vLLM, for example `llama3.1:8b`, `qwen2.5:14b`, `mistral-nemo:12b`. Passing a model
no healthy node advertises returns `503` with code `no_capacity` — and you are not charged,
because the challenge is issued before routing.

## Other endpoints

- `GET /v1/nodes` — registered compute nodes, their health, and their advertised models. Free.
- `GET /v1/settlements` — the two-legged USDC settlement audit trail. Free.
- `GET /healthz` — liveness. Free.
- `GET /readyz` — readiness, per-dependency. Free.
- `GET /.well-known/x402` — this service's machine-readable discovery manifest. Free.
- `POST /v1/nodes/register`, `POST /v1/nodes/{nodeId}/heartbeat` — for GPU operators joining the
  mesh, not for inference clients. Ed25519-signed by the operator key.

## Discovery

- Discovery manifest: https://mesh.example.com/.well-known/x402
- This file: https://mesh.example.com/llms.txt
- OpenAPI 3.1 description: https://mesh.example.com/openapi.yaml
- Discovery tags: `x402-global-challenge`, `ai`, `inference`, `llm`, `algorand`
- Also listed in the x402 Bazaar via the `bazaar` discovery extension, so
  `client.extensions.bazaar.search({ query: "llm inference" })` will find it.

## Networks

Canonical CAIP-2 identifiers (the 32-character truncated genesis hash form):

- MainNet `algorand:wGHE2Pwdvd7S12BL5FaOP20EGYesN73k`, USDC asset id `31566704`
- TestNet `algorand:SGO1GKSzyE7IEPItTxCByw9x8FmnrCDe`, USDC asset id `10458941`

The facilitator advertises the same two chains using the full padded genesis hash
(`algorand:wGHE2Pwdvd7S12BL5FaOP20EGYesN73ktiC1qzkkit8=`). Both encodings name the same chain;
this service accepts either on input and always emits the canonical form.

Facilitator: https://facilitator.goplausible.xyz

## Errors

Every error is `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details"? } }`. Codes you may see:
`validation_error` (400), `auth_error` (401), `payment_error` (402), `rate_limited` (429),
`internal_error` (500), `upstream_error` / `settlement_error` (502), `no_capacity` (503).
Retrying a `no_capacity` after a few seconds is reasonable; retrying a `validation_error` is not.
